lesson_title: Delta, Dials and the Ghost Root: Algebra, Functions and Trig Essentials
hook_text: The algebra says x = 2. The equation says NO. Meet the ghost root.
clip_script: And the surd equation carries a sting. Root of x plus seven equals x minus five. Square both sides: x plus seven equals x squared minus ten x plus twenty-five, so x squared minus eleven x plus eighteen equals zero — x equals nine or x equals two. Now the compulsory check: x equals nine gives root sixteen, four, and nine minus five, four — valid. X equals two gives root nine, three, but two minus five is minus three — invalid. Squaring manufactures ghost solutions, and the check is not politeness; it is part of the method.
visual_style: Two candidate answers walk toward the original equation like a border checkpoint; x equals nine shows matching stamps, four and four, and passes; x equals two flashes three versus minus three, turns translucent and dissolves — a ghost caught at the gate.
mood: Ghost-story reveal — the answer that algebra invented and the original equation refuses.
pacing: Brisk squaring and factorising, slow-down at the checkpoint, sharp dissolve on the ghost, confident close.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision lesson and send every ghost root home before the marker meets it.
